newsitem.title: JAPAN: Citizen says won't change outlook over forex level.
newsitem.headline: Citizen says won't change outlook over forex level.

text.p: Japan's Citizen Watch Co Ltd said on Monday that the current dollar/yen level will not lead to a major change in the company's business outlook for the 1997/98 business year.
President Hiroshi Haruta told reporters that the company's foreign currency exposure has diminished and the impact on its business has become smaller.
"I don't see any major change in our business outlook (1997/98) due to currencies," he said.

Asked about the impact of the current yen/dollar level on its business, a spokesman told the same briefing the company made its latest earnings estimate based on an assumption the dollar would stay at 120 yen to the dollar, but added that even if the dollar fluctuates at the current level of around 115 yen, the company does not see any major impact on its business outlook.

In early June, Citizen predicted a 2.4 percent increase in its group net profits to 10 billion yen for 1997/98. The leading Japanese watchmaker enjoyed nearly 30 percent growth in its profit in the previous business year.

The president said the company had no plans at the moment to increase its dividend payout this business year, but said it hoped to raise the return on equity (ROE) to a double-digit level in the medium term from the current level of around five percent.
But he added that increasing the ROE was not the company's top priority.

The company is considering introducing a netting system for internal foreign exchange settlements after April 1 next year, when Japan eases its controls on foreign exchange transactions, a company official said. The move would allow the company to save money by not having to pay bank commissions, he said.
